page.running_head: Justinus Thrax & Tiberius II. Lib. III.

main_text.p: Constantinopolin, ad Senatus Rom. infantiam contumeliosa nec fine periculo revocatio in ca[?] fa, quam Longini, qui primus interillos Ravennæ præfides, qui imperatoris nomine ibi jus reddebant, & bella administrabant, & propriæa Exarchi dicebantur miffio fubleccuta eft, Narses quippe, odio & metu exagitatus; Longobardos quorum conductitia opera contra Gothos ulterat in Italiam ipse regni sibi idem constituendi cavit, & per eos eam telam orsus est, quam revera necSophia, quæ Narsen tanquam Eunuchum aulæ dividendam in Gyneceo penfa vocaverat, nec ritus ejus Justinus detexere poterant. Scilicet Alboinus, Longobardorum Rex, Saxonibus in societatem adscitus, & fed bus fuis Hunnis & Avaris cum conditione traditus, in Italiam venit, primo mò Vincentiam & Veronam, mox, deditionem fuadentes Episcopo, Mediolanum, tandem Tici-num poft triennii obfidionem cepit, & regno intra Alpes, mare Ligusticum, & Apenninum rexit. Ei, dolore Rolimundæ conjugis ex stupro patris sui Cunimundi Regis Gepidarum, ab Alboino boino occisi, bibere coactæ ab Helmichilde vel Peredio quodam ... lucceffit Cleph, qui ... etfi XVIII menses tantum regnavit, ... rum Cornelli abarce, quâ contra Ravennates ... lud munivit, Insula deinceps dictum, ... fecit. Post hæc ... Ariulfus ... ta XXX Ducum, quæ tamen ultra decennium non durabit, sed per discordiam eorum ... regius dominatus, sub XX ordine ... Quæ contra Gallos egere, in Gallicis ... hostimeo addi poteft, Arsaber Longobardorum Duces.
Varnefrid de gestis Longobardorum lib. 2. cap. 31.

page.notes: Page is a scan with heavy show-through and faint, partly illegible text, especially in the right half and at the line ends; many words are reconstructed and uncertain. The marginal notes at left are only partly legible. Bleed-through from the reverse side obscures lines near the centre-right.
